_why: HB10160 was referred to committee on 2026-08-27, congress.gov carried its introduced text that day, and govblock said 'No text on file yet' for five days. Neither existing pipeline could have caught it: dp-us-native dies on an undeclared fast-xml-parser, and the nightly LegiScan and text deltas run on box 1 and write to Neon, which the site no longer reads. This one writes to Aurora, which it does.
_pace: 120 ms between calls. One night's window is ~850 changed bills and came in at 829 requests in 3.4 minutes against a 20,000/hour ceiling — about 4% of it. The .htm bodies come from www.congress.gov rather than the API and take no key; they are paced the same.
_scope: The 119th, by updateDate, re-reading a day of overlap so a crash mid-run leaves no hole. A full-congress backfill is the same script with --all. Only the text families: the version list, the .htm body, the Documents link. Actions, cosponsors, committees, subjects and related bills are the same walk with more endpoints and are added on top of this.
_credentials: Resolved at run time from the cluster's own MasterUserSecret, not from a file. Aurora's master credentials are RDS-managed and rotate every 7 days: the migration staged them at 08:06Z on 2026-09-01, they rotated at 12:21Z, and every box-side job that used them failed password authentication from then on — silently, because the site reaches Aurora through the Data API with the secret's ARN and never noticed. CONGRESS_API_KEY comes from .env.local, which run-due already passes with --env-file.
_deliberately_not_fetched: The PDF and USLM renderings of each version. The Formatted Text .htm is what htmlToText was written against and what the bill page renders; the other two are the same words in packaging the site has no reader for. A govinfo row is never replaced either — it came from the XML, which carries the amendment marks the .htm has already flattened, so this fills gaps and refreshes only its own.
_steps: sync: the API by updateDate, for text that moved. billstatus: the eight govinfo zips, 51 MB and no API calls, for summaries, titles, related bills and the bill each amendment and committee report belongs to — linkage the API's list endpoints do not carry at all. harvest: the ten API families, 64 requests, with committee-meeting detail bounded to the recently-updated.
